messages:
alice: kicking off a gradual rollout for the structured-output / function-calling feature. plan = enable server flag `feat_structured_output_v1` at 10% traffic in us-west-2 canary. client SDKs will send header `X-Redwood-Fncall: compat-v1`. any blockers?

sam: sgtm. confirm that clients default to legacy behavior if they don't send the header?

alice: yes — server will auto-fallback to text-generation when header missing or if compatibility mode=legacy. we should also gate tool execution behind an opt-in flag per customer.

jess: +1. request: disable outbound tool execution for the initial canary (keep structured JSON only). i'll add an integration test for tool suppression.

mike: a couple of guardrails to add: 1) payload size cap (<= 64KB) for structured output during canary, 2) error-rate rollback threshold at 0.5% over a 5m window, 3) telemetry tag rollout=fncall-canary.

alice: noted. adding config snippet for ops to apply:
```
feature_flags:
  feat_structured_output_v1:
    enabled: true
    rollout_percent: 10
    regions: ["us-west-2"]
    options:
      allow_tool_calls: false
      max_payload_bytes: 65536
      compat_mode_header: "X-Redwood-Fncall"
      compat_values: ["compat-v1", "legacy"]
      rollback_on_error_rate: 0.005
      telemetry_tag: "rollout=fncall-canary"
```

sam: i'll coordinate with SDK team to add header handling. proposed client behavior: send header with version, if server responds with `X-Redwood-Fncall-Ack: strict` then enable strict structured parsing, otherwise continue fallback. also will add opt-in flag in SDK: `enableFncallStructured = false` by default for GA.

jess: can you also publish a small example for customers? something like:
```http
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer ...
  X-Redwood-Fncall: compat-v1
Body:
  {"prompt": "...", "response_format": "structured"}
```

mike: add a note to watch model hallucinations on tool-calls — supply a regression eval set. i'll set up a datadog monitor: `fncall.error_rate` and `fncall.hallucination_score` (experimental). rollback if either crosses threshold.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag `feat_structured_output_v1` rolled out to canary group in us-west-2 on instances [r-infer-1,r-infer-2,r-infer-3].

qa-bot: qa: running smoke + safety checks now. will post results in 30m.

alice: quick checklist for this canary:
- SDK header handling added (sam)
- server flag + ops rollout (ops/devops)
- disable tool execution in canary (jess)
- payload cap + error rollback (mike)
- telemetry and monitors (mike)
- e2e tests + example docs (jess/sam)

sam: pinging @sdk-team channel to prioritize header update & fallback. i'll link PR when ready.

jess: started a PR for the server-side validation tests: https://git.company/repo/pull/402 (adding e2e + a case for missing header -> legacy flow).

mike: monitor created: `fncall.canary.errors > 0.5% for 5m` and alert to #eng-oncall. also added a playbook step: immediate rollback and notify owners.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment health check passed at +10m. cpu/latency within baseline.

qa-bot: qa: smoke passed. found one edge-case with empty tool list -> server responded 500 for one request. filing bug ticket.

alice: thanks — @jess can you triage the 500? if it's quick patch we can keep canary running, otherwise rollback.

jess: seen it, looks like null serialization bug in the tool-handling code. patching now.

mike: we should also tag logs with `rollout_id=fncall-canary-2026-02` to trace incidents.

alice: agreed. final note: if stable for 1h with no regressions we'll bump to 30% and re-enable limited tool calls (still with payload cap). :thumbsup:

sam: i'll post SDK PR link once CI passes.

jess: patch merged, restarted canary instances.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: patch applied, instances restarted. health OK.

alice: canary healthy at +45m, no major regressions. increasing to 30% in 15m unless anyone objects. :shipit:

mike: watching monitors. go ahead.

qa-bot: full regression suite queued as part of the 30% increase. will report failures to this thread.

alice: thanks team — keeping this thread as the coordination channel. we'll open a postmortem if anything goes wrong.
